title: Tooling Bank: custody and digital twins for every OEM-owned casting pattern, triggered by foundry closures
deciding_reason: TAM is bounded by roughly 45 foundry closures a year, foundries store tooling free, OEM tooling platforms exist, and printed sand erodes the need for patterns.

title: Second-Source Factory: sell approved part numbers, not consulting hours
deciding_reason: Primes own the approval gate and are hiring in-house; free government substitutes cover DLA parts; no evidence primes will buy a third-party package, which is the idea's own kill test.

title: Tier-Three Credit: lend against the prime's payment and the customer's tooling, not the foundry's balance sheet
deciding_reason: Incumbent supply chain finance and PO lenders already target this gap, the prime-sponsored structure is unproven, and the revenue test needs a roughly $830M book.

title: Foundry BOT: build, staff, operate and transfer foundries for the new buyers who cannot hire the people
deciding_reason: Net fee revenue is small and lumpy, turnkey incumbents exist, and the named buyers are building their own teams.

title: The Non-GE Foundry: customer-funded independent castings capacity for everyone who just lost a neutral supplier
deciding_reason: Genuine $100M+ prize, but capital-heavy, incumbents and SpaceX are already spending, the neutral-supplier premise is mostly false, and first parts would arrive after the shortage window.

title: US-Pour: the verified melt-and-pour ledger that turns 'made from US steel' into a 25-to-40-point tariff cut
deciding_reason: Volatile rule, unmeasured and probably tiny qualifying pool, and melt-and-pour reporting is already mandated and built into broker software.

title: Cleaning Room as a Service: we run the foundry's finishing department and bill per casting
deciding_reason: Price exceeds value: foundries self-build cells for about $25k and vendors sell them, so a $250k cell-year managed service has no buyer logic.

title: One Approved Supplier, Two Hundred Foundries: the supplier of record that CT-screens before machining and guarantees good parts
deciding_reason: CT screening does not work on heavy ferrous castings, buyers can already order machined castings, Hadrian is better funded and integrated, and $100M is pass-through revenue at thin margins.

title: Spare-Set Pool: hot-section outages with a guaranteed return-to-service date
deciding_reason: Rotor exchange and hot-gas-path component exchange are already sold by GE, Hanwha, MD&A and EthosEnergy; the remaining lease-with-guarantee gap is thin, capital-heavy and needs 20%+ share of reachable events.

title: Hot-Section Core Exchange (LKQ for turbines)
deciding_reason: GE and every ISP already run exchange or trade-in programs, owners repair and return their own parts instead of selling cores, and the LKQ flow of scrapped assets does not exist here. Ceiling about $25M.

title: Certified Unfired: the grading and escrow layer for stranded turbines and slot reservations (collectibles liquidity stack)
deciding_reason: A handful of deals, OEM refurbishment already provides the 'grade', OEM consent is the key dependency, and the principal version is a cyclical dealer with no moat. Exposed to an AI-capex pullback.

title: Outage Bench: a credentialed bench of turbine specialists (expert-labor marketplace plus spot labor)
deciding_reason: A commodity staffing business that the idea itself calls the weakest moat; competitors exist, and the credential that would make it defensible has no evidence of acceptance. Fails the 'path to something that scales' rule.

title: Progressive for Turbines: a condition-priced, insurer-backed independent LTSA
deciding_reason: Only idea whose arithmetic reaches $100M at 3-5% share with an existing budget line and an unproductised pricing/risk wrapper. Weaknesses: ISPs already sell F-class LTSAs, OEM can match price, casting scarcity cuts both ways, ceiling about $70M.

title: Hot-Section Repair Factory: automated multi-cycle repair the OEM would rather replace than do
deciding_reason: Incumbents are well-capitalized roll-ups with the same capacity problem and the same automation toolkit; automation is not a moat and the metallurgy premise is shaky. Capital-heavy business with thin differentiation.

title: Megawatts from existing iron: financed, multi-vendor uprates paid from capacity revenue
deciding_reason: Market is small (~200 MW per auction), served by OEMs and in-house IPP teams, depends on a capacity price collar that ends after 2029/30, and an accredited-MW guarantee is not controllable. Ceiling about $30M.

title: Uptime Wrapper for mixed behind-the-meter data-center gas fleets
deciding_reason: Demand is real but addressable owners either self-operate or buy power-as-a-service that bundles O&M; OEMs and dealers cover most boxes. A pure wrapper without owned assets is a services niche with ceiling about $35M.

title: Harvest Pit Crew
deciding_reason: Deere and dealers already run free harvest-run vans and parts trailers; crews self-repair; the buyer pool is a few hundred crews; the fee approaches the crew's whole repair bill. Too small and partly done.

title: Shared Shop
deciding_reason: Revenue is mostly pass-through cost, the buyer must give up its own techs, and dealers already sell on-site contracts. Gross profit at the idea's own ceiling is $15-20M.

title: Machine Passport
deciding_reason: Lender valuation and inspections already exist, prices are 4-10x the market, and the best-funded peer is tiny. Useful as a feeder dataset for a warranty product, not a $100M business alone.

title: Tech Bench
deciding_reason: Priced 2.5x above market wages, no moat by the idea's own admission, a staffing margin, and existing ag recruiters. Even a good outcome is a $30M staffing business.

title: Any-Shop Plan
deciding_reason: Structurally the most scalable (balance sheet, lender distribution) but crowded, priced at combine rather than blended levels, and the math lands near $25-40M revenue unless attach reaches about 11% of the base.

title: Standard Shop
deciding_reason: A parts-distribution margin business at heroic wallet share, squeezed by Deere's price cuts and second-tier parts, with a PE-backed multi-state supplier already serving independents.

title: Core Bank
deciding_reason: Best structure in the set (core stream as moat), but the event math contradicts itself, OEM reman and a PE-backed 42-location rebuilder already hold the core stream, and independent rebuilders compete on price.

title: Elevator Depots
deciding_reason: Revenue is gross sales, not net; first-party supply is open to every retailer; dealers and Deere already stock parts on or near the farm. A $20M GMV, single-digit-million net business.

title: The Tele-Inspection Factory
deciding_reason: Already built: Inspected has 100k+ Florida virtual inspections, a Series A, and Broward access since Aug 2025, with under $10M revenue. Low statutory barrier means no moat, and 1.7M inspections is about 28x the leader.

title: Inspection-as-a-Service for the Top Homebuilders
deciding_reason: Builder-paid private-provider inspections are already 25-35% of inspections in sample Florida counties. Reaching $100M needs about a third of reachable-state homes, and the defect-data premium is a few hundred dollars per home.

title: Technical Control plus Latent-Defect Warranty for Attached Housing (an NHBC for the U.S.)
deciding_reason: Tiny, legislation-dependent pool: Colorado condo output is in the tens to low hundreds of units, Washington is not a second market, and the incumbent warranty leader earns under $700 per home versus the $2,800 required.

title: The Platform Behind Independent Private Providers
deciding_reason: Gross-to-net kills it: the idea itself calls $450M gross heroic, the employee rule favors hiring firms over platforms, and no evidence independents want a 22% take.

title: Fixed-Price Special Inspection and Closeout
deciding_reason: Share math is plausible but it is a labor business against $1B incumbents who can already quote lump sum; remote review does not remove the on-site technician, and the closeout-date value is an untested insider claim.

title: Permit-Clean: Verified Permit Status and Closeout at the Closing Table
deciding_reason: Unsourced incidence, existing lien-search workflow, aggregator data already for sale, and a statute that eases the problem. The cure work belongs to contractors, so revenue is a thin referral margin on a small pool.

title: The Shot-Clock Concession
deciding_reason: The concession model is SAFEbuilt's, built over two decades and 19 acquisitions. The clock guarantee is the only novelty and is untested; procurement is slow and the fee pool shrinks as private-provider volume grows.

title: Energize-on-Schedule: Inspection, Commissioning and AHJ Desk for Hyperscaler Build Programs
deciding_reason: Narrow buyer set, funded commissioning roll-ups already exist, and a date guarantee depends on power and AHJs outside the vendor's control. The idea's own path needs 7-13% of a $0.75-1.5B pool.

title: Swap, Don't Buy: AMI-driven redeployment of the installed transformer base
deciding_reason: Avoided purchase ($2-3k) is about the cost of the two truck rolls a swap needs, upsizing costs only about $196, and four vendors already sell the analytics. Value per swap is near zero.

title: Cores for Coils: a closed-loop second-life factory for retired distribution transformers
deciding_reason: Already done by Maddox, RESA and a PE-backed 1,600-person Sunbelt Solomon; DOE says the rebuild market is historically small, labor-limited and its recent uptick is temporary. Only automated winding is a real wedge.

title: Gavi for Transformers: a take-or-pay buyers' consortium that underwrites standard-spec capacity
deciding_reason: The best-organized buyers already pool through RESCO/UUS/ERMCO, DOE gives spec standardization away, and a 6-9% distributor margin cannot support a venture-scale company without a financing spread that belongs to CFC/CoBank.

title: TSMC for Transformer Cores: a neutral, automated core-and-coil foundry
deciding_reason: A neutral core supplier already exists and is doubling (Tempel, Cogent), OEMs keep cores captive, and the one US GOES mill is a competitor with a defense contract. Capital-heavy with pass-through revenue.

title: Time-to-Power Fleet: build-to-stock multi-ratio substation transformers for whoever signs the interconnection first
deciding_reason: Strongest demand story, but the fleet needs scarce OEM slots, utility spec acceptance is unproven, four funded or PE-backed players already sell stock, leases or modular units, and new capacity lands in 2027-28 against a $0.85B fleet.

title: Time-to-Restore Cover: parametric outage insurance plus spares access for owners nobody covers
deciding_reason: Revenue is a fraction of a premium pool the idea itself says would need 28-40% share; low failure base rate caps losses; parametric and spare-pool competitors already cover the pieces.

title: Achilles for the Grid: the supplier-paid, accredited trust network under Executive Order 14420
deciding_reason: Real mandate, but rules are unwritten, DOE may run a free list, Fortress already owns utility vendor-risk with $125M, and the order mainly bites on China-linked gear. Ceiling hinges on DOE choosing accredited assessors.

title: Virtual Transformers: buy capacity from the installed fleet instead of the factory
deciding_reason: No one guarantees MVA, but OEMs, Doble and monitoring vendors sell every component, funded startups compete for the same speed-to-power budget, and $100M needs thousands of uprate jobs a year in a services-heavy model.

title: Capital Projects Desk: the financeable-package standard for association repairs
deciding_reason: Size premise is false: real Phase-2 repair permits average $337k-$496k, not $3M, so Florida managed construction is about $0.25B a year (a 4% fee is about $10M), and owner's-rep firms already sell this service.

title: Living reserve study: the annual, lender-accepted reserve record (Fannie's three-year clause)
deciding_reason: A direct incumbent already sells the 'living' study, and the premise fails: lenders need a study under three years old, which a normal update satisfies, so annual pricing exceeds the value delivered.

title: Ledger-underwritten association credit (CondoConta for the US)
deciding_reason: The structural insight (banks lend for deposits) is real, but demand is smaller than assumed, managers' captive desks own the channel, and deposit-funded banks beat a warehouse-funded non-bank on price. Gross revenue plausibly tops out near $35M.

title: Association treasury: project-funds escrow, draw and instant-pay rail
deciding_reason: A feature, not a company: payments, reserve ladders and draw periods each have an owner (Vantaca Vendor Pay, HOA Invest, association banks), and the $103M path sums thin fees on an inflated flow base.

title: Fee-only board CFO: conflict-free cost recovery for associations
deciding_reason: The conflict thesis is legitimate and legally supported, but each savings leg has a funded incumbent or captive program, success fees are hard to attribute, and the realistic fee pool is low-tens of millions.

title: Manager-of-record for small and self-managed associations
deciding_reason: An AI-plus-licensed-manager services roll-up with a funded YC competitor, a cheap profitable software substitute for self-managed boards, and license-bound leverage; the idea itself notes it matches a flagged cliche.

title: Assessment deferral: pay the association in full, collect from the owner at sale
deciding_reason: Legal path exists but the business needs about $150M of equity for $30-40M of net interest, competes with cheaper association-level loans and public programs, and adversely selects troubled buildings. Ceiling about $25M.

title: Neutral association data exchange with an indemnified lender desk
deciding_reason: Best structural fit to the shock, but CondoSafe, InspectHOA, RealPage and free GSE tools already cover it, the per-project wallet is capped, and the indemnity is regulated insurance. A network-standard bet with a ceiling near $20M.

title: Pre-Op Lock: ancillary network check at prior authorization
deciding_reason: Vendors earn far more through IDR than any benchmark-linked SCA, so lever 1 fails; neuro volume was overstated 2.4x; Zelis and network teams own the channel. Honest ceiling is a niche analytics/consulting product.

title: Sponsor Desk: the employer's own IDR control tower
deciding_reason: Genuine mandate and no sponsor software, but buyers act through brokers and TPAs who hold the data; reachable lives times $5 gives low tens of millions, not $100M.

title: Lockstep: employer master agreements with the ten big filers
deciding_reason: Counterparties' alternative (85% win at ~445% of QPA) beats the proposed rate card; ERIC reports offers far above market; no evidence the big filers want a floor-setting coalition deal.

title: Float: seven-day pay against contract-rate receivables
deciding_reason: Collateral enforceability just worsened; biggest filers need no financing; the contract-receivable leg depends on dead Lockstep; a lender needs ~$685M capital for $100M revenue.

title: Cold Open: neutral price opinion and settlement inside open negotiation
deciding_reason: Payer-paid negotiation is already done at scale; no evidence a filer winning 85% at ~445% of QPA would accept a neutral's range; portal why-now lands in 2027-28; 15% take-up is heroic.

title: Guild: group-owned IDR and contracting mutual for independent groups
deciding_reason: Crowded, legally exposed provider-side segment with scaled incumbents; mutual structure adds no scale advantage; $100M needs ~20% of the pool.

title: Plumb Line: QPA-of-record after TMA III
deciding_reason: Most regime-robust idea, but the comparable neutral benchmark earns ~$37M, Zelis already ships QPA analytics, and no recompute mandate with a deadline exists yet.

title: Gavel: an AI-native, ownership-clean certified IDR entity
deciding_reason: Providers pick the entity and pick provider-favorable ones; a clean, calibrated entity gets only the randomized remainder (~$13M). Certification is not the barrier; selection is.

title: Zero-Down Copper Exit: pay for the cutover out of the phone bill
deciding_reason: Real mandate and budget line, but the owner-side managed program is already sold by MarketSpark, Ooma and Alarm.com; the $100M needs more than the leader's own stated goal.

title: Wire-Center Sweeps: convert every unconverted small system in a retiring footprint, one visit each
deciding_reason: Demand arrives in small rural pockets and is already served by the monitoring dealer; cold-canvass CAC for a commodity swap cannot support a $100M path.

title: Second-Opinion Desk: free quote checks that become the owner's neutral fire-and-life-safety program
deciding_reason: A 40-year-old independent incumbent (Telgian) shows the model tops out near $100M of revenue, and the entrant would be thin-margin pass-through.

title: Panel Liberation: zero-down replacement of locked proprietary fire panels
deciding_reason: Lock-in is narrow (mostly Simplex), the work is ordinary bid-out capital construction, and there is no scalable moat.

title: Full-Service Fire Protection: one flat price per square foot a year, repairs included
deciding_reason: Flat-fee comprehensive fire service is already sold (JCI, public full-service specs), and the revenue per building is overstated by 2-3x.

title: Impairment Desk: the first four hours after any fire system goes out of service
deciding_reason: Insurers, dealers and guard firms already own each silo, and the idea's own condition for survival (AHJ log data showing the event count) is unmet.

title: Hyperscale Life-Safety Crew: the scarce-trade play behind the data-center build
deciding_reason: Real demand, but it is an operating contractor business competing with funded primes for the same scarce labor, with no data, software or network moat.

title: Hood-to-Alarm Program for restaurant franchise systems
deciding_reason: The bundling gap is real but the ticket is small, the leader is a $74M system, and filing and compliance records already run through Brycer.

title: Retro-Flag: post-adjudication 340B correction rail for state Medicaid
deciding_reason: Real gap on the state side, but the pool is small, politically contested by hospitals, locked behind Gainwell, and one simple state ban removes the need for a vendor.

title: Route Desk: per-unit 340B / MFP / non-340B router for health systems
deciding_reason: Real shock and a CFO budget, but a one-rule, mostly one-time optimization that incumbents and consultants can copy, capped near $30M.

title: Cass for 340B: audit-and-pay hub for drug purchases, fees and remittances
deciding_reason: Hospital-side contingency recovery already exists, the leak rate is unmeasured, the float needs a balance sheet, and $100M needs heroic share.

title: Switzerland: hospital-governed, manufacturer-funded 340B claims trust
deciding_reason: Neutrality is a real insight, but the buyer picks the platform and the only big pot is a single federal contract under unpassed bills.

title: Open TPA: 340B administrator with no pharmacy attached
deciding_reason: Flat-fee and independent TPAs already exist, the lock-in sits with chain pharmacies, and the realistic share is small.

title: JG-Day for Payers: 340B cut pass-through desk for non-conflicted Medicare Advantage plans
deciding_reason: A modifier edit and contract language are features plans do themselves; the buyers are the plans with the strongest in-house teams.

title: Specialty Door: shared specialty pharmacy utility for health systems
deciding_reason: Shields already aggregates over a third of health systems with new Evernorth backing, so the shared-scale insight is the incumbent's pitch.

title: Pigeonhole: IRA MFP-versus-340B duplicate-discount floor for manufacturers
deciding_reason: Best-argued idea with a funded buyer, but few buyers, an incumbent just consolidated, and the recovery path is legally uncertain.

title: Clean Exit: sponsor-level cell captives built to be sold with the company
deciding_reason: Real pain but the veto premise is unsupported, exit tools are already standard, sponsors adopt portfolio programs once or twice a decade, and short holds undercut captives.

title: The 12th Member: a cross-agency fill-rate machine for group captives
deciding_reason: The gap is already filled by open heterogeneous captives and a dominant incumbent; $100M needs about a fifth of future market premium.

title: Zero-Collateral Cell Reinsurer: a pooled $250M reinsurer that qualifies for the U.S. no-collateral rule
deciding_reason: Legal premise appears broken (RJ scope excludes captive classes), fronts keep contractual discretion, and no pilot is possible before $250M of capital.

title: The 97% Book: buy the agencies and managers that sponsor group captives
deciding_reason: Already being done by funded rivals; it is a capital-allocation trade, not a gap, and the arbitrage is priced by competing buyers.

title: Pareto TPA: paid on the 7% of claims that carry 40% of the cost
deciding_reason: Savings-share fees are legally restricted in at least one major self-insured state and Paradigm already sells outcome-priced large-claim management; the niche stays small.

title: Retained-Risk Bureau: the NCCI of captives, self-insureds and large deductibles
deciding_reason: Cold-start give-to-get pool with thin buyer wallet and existing manager and TPA-built benchmarks.

title: Broker Mutual: a member-owned liability RRG that underwrites every freight load
deciding_reason: Best shock in the pool but the premium pool is about 3x smaller than assumed, Marsh already supplies rated paper, and an unrated RRG carries verdict tail on thin capital.

title: The TPA Captive: stop-loss captives sponsored by the people who see the claims first
deciding_reason: Real pricing pain (Segal +12.7%) but crowded with consultants and carriers, no TPA appetite for insurance risk evidenced, and tightening reinsurance capacity.

title: Ready-to-Build: the constraint-clearing layer for line crews
deciding_reason: Real pain, but the only scaled analog (Locusview) is ~3x cheaper per crew, already on 4,000+ crews, and now owned by Itron; $100M needs 3x pricing or half the market.

title: Zero-Redline: outcome-priced distribution work packages
deciding_reason: Outcome pricing is a real wedge nobody sells, but software owners (Enverus, Itron), entrenched design firms and funded AI-native entrants cap this services model near $60M.

title: Spec Passport: shared product qualification, paid by the suppliers
deciding_reason: The co-op wedge is already served by a free federal acceptance list, IOUs will not cede liability, and the qualification-fee pool is invented; ceiling ~$30M.

title: Capacity Upgrade Desk: limiting-element-first reconductoring, funded by the load
deciding_reason: Neutral advice and EPC economics cannot coexist, the fee path needs ~21% of all reconductored miles, and the upside is a ~$60M consultancy.

title: Accredited Delivery Partner: customer-funded connections at the customer's speed
deciding_reason: A general contractor wedge: big jobs bypass the standard path, Quanta-owned contractors already do it, state patchwork limits scale, and net revenue is ~$8-18M even at $100M gross.

title: Pooled Crews: a contract vehicle with reserved crews for co-ops and munis
deciding_reason: Pooled purchasing, co-op-owned crews and generalist vehicles already exist; RUS rules force co-op-level contracts; $100M needs 14-33% of the pool and contractors will not hold crews for unpaid demand.

title: Pre-Accepted Substations for non-hyperscaler load
deciding_reason: Only pool that can carry $100M, but that is gross pass-through (~$12-15M net), the standards library is available on request, and OEM turnkey plus a funded a16z entrant are already selling it; median under $20M.

title: Make-Ready Rail: the bulk pole-application exchange
deciding_reason: Wrong regulator for the California wedge, co-op and municipal poles exempt from FCC clocks, and owner-side and engineering incumbents already serve both sides; even 100% of BEAD is ~$80M a year of fees.

title: Shop Ledger: cross-shop carrier-health network, paid in 24 hours
deciding_reason: cbCharge has done 24-hour pay with fleet credit risk since 1995 and already holds the cross-shop ledger; the ELD score is a feature incumbents can copy, and $100M exceeds Fullbay's whole installed base.

title: Overnight Yard Crews: Level-1 PM and tire crews with remote master techs
deciding_reason: Labor-capped services business in a space Ryder, Love's and a PE roll-up are consolidating; $100M needs 3x Ryder's mobile tech base and the inspection rules narrow the Level-1 scope.

title: Pay-by-the-Mile: major-repair credit repaid through the factor and the odometer
deciding_reason: Crowded with four named financing products, unit economics negative on the idea's own numbers, and the upside stays under $50M.

title: Warranty Wrapper: the OEM-paid multi-brand network for non-dealer warranty and campaign work
deciding_reason: The $3.94B pool is two-thirds farm and construction equipment, Love's already does multi-OEM non-dealer warranty with claims filing, and telematics vendors are absorbing the claim workflow.

title: Uptime Plan: cost-per-mile maintenance for the fleet the lessors and OEMs ignore
deciding_reason: Ryder, Penske, FleetNet and NTP already sell outsourced maintenance on customer-owned mixed-make trucks; the unique piece (small old fleets, ELD pricing) has an unsolved distribution and adverse-selection problem.

title: Public Fleet Bench: fixed-fee maintenance for fleets that cannot pay market wages
deciding_reason: A funded national incumbent (First Student) already sells maintenance-only to districts, contracts are about $1.3M each, and most of the revenue is parts pass-through.

title: Second Source: graded, warrantied used and reman power-train parts plus a core exchange
deciding_reason: A mature, OEM-dominated category with salvage and independent rebuilders already present; plausible volume but thin margins, no technology moat, and the upside stays under $100M.

title: Aftertreatment Exchange: pooled, multi-brand DPF/DOC/SCR swap units
deciding_reason: OEM exchange at 800+ locations, dealer same-day cleaning, a licensed cleaning network and fleets' in-house shops already cover it; the swap barely beats a few hours of cleaning and the upside is about $35M.

title: Clock-Out Capital: visit-level Medicaid finance priced on recoupment
deciding_reason: Financed-balance pool is too small for a $667M book, incumbents already advance 85%, and true-sale factoring is barred; upside tops out near $55M.

title: The exception-free fiscal intermediary
deciding_reason: Mandated state spend with a named signer, no free substitute, live precedent and rebid wave, and a believable ~85k-participant or NY-class path to $100M.

title: Proof-of-Visit: the verification rail for home care
deciding_reason: EVV owners already hold both visit and payroll data, per-visit pricing is unsupported, and the savings-share route rests on one disputed NY number; upside near $45M.

title: Personal-care administrator for fee-for-service states (the NEMT-broker model)
deciding_reason: The 3-5% fee premise is contradicted by observed 0.5-2% state admin fees; even the upside is small.

title: The neutral LTSS manager for plans that compete with Elevance
deciding_reason: Demonstrated demand and a $2.7B exit comp, plan budgets that already paid for this, a fresh competitor-ownership shock, and a believable top-decile path to ~$100M.

title: Risk and Mobility MGA for home care agencies
deciding_reason: Premium pool is far smaller than assumed, so $100M needs a heroic share, and a national home-care MGA program already exists.

title: Continuity Bench: pooled W-2 aides for the TPS and fill-rate gap
deciding_reason: Price exceeds value ($4 spread on a $19 hour) and the bottleneck is labor supply and pay, not pooling; funded W-2 competitors exist.

title: Partner-not-buy network for independent agencies
deciding_reason: No payer-contract uplift exists in state-set Medicaid rates and a 5% fee exceeds owners' margins; even the upside is small.

title: Grease Elevator
deciding_reason: Real asset, but volume is capped near the independent pool, merchant spreads are 1-3c not 5c, and Eco-Energy, Neste and traders already operate the model. Top-decile net revenue is about $60M.

title: Bankable Supply
deciding_reason: Balance-sheet traders and banks already provide supply paper to financed independents; a startup is not the credit lenders want, and the customer set is about 30-40 projects.

title: Cleared Lot
deciding_reason: Inspection, QAP defense and contract clauses already do most of the job; the warranty is the only new piece and its premium is the insurer's revenue. Top-decile net is about $35M.

title: Oil Yield Partner
deciding_reason: Real yield gap, but revenue-share extraction has precedent, OEMs and enzymes compete, self-funding plants simply buy, and 40 plants is a heroic share of the addressable set.

title: Second Stream
deciding_reason: The customer can buy the hardware, the grease is worth far less than assumed, and PE-backed pumpers and Restaurant Technologies own the stops. Top-decile about $45M.

title: Oil Check
deciding_reason: The model already runs at farmer-owned crushers, the reachable crush is about a fifth of the market, and the big three profit from flat pricing. Even the upside is about $20M.

title: Co-Pro Desk
deciding_reason: Wrong RIN class, no 45Z, Phillips 66 walked away, integrated majors do it in-house, and the idea's own unit economics are thin. Upside is about $30M.

title: Premium Ledger
deciding_reason: Key input (FD-CIC) does not cover waste lipids, Veriflux already traces them, and the $114M path needs near-total share. The idea itself calls it closest to dead.

title: Siap Masak: certified cook-ready prep plants for 4-hour kitchens
deciding_reason: A centralised plant is exactly the structure BGN is policing: eligible sellers are micro, small and cooperative only, supplier concentration is sanctioned, and the incumbent integrators already hold the chicken lane.

title: Satu Faktur: kecamatan consolidation hubs in idle Kopdes cold stores
deciding_reason: Policy-aligned, but the operator layer is pre-empted by Agrinas, Bulog, Pos and Telkom, the BGN portal does the single-PO job, and the fee is capped.

title: Franchisor-in-a-box for the institutional operator groups
deciding_reason: Four to six buyers, about 2,500 reachable kitchens, in-house HQ logistics, and a procurement-margin model that is the commission regulators are chasing.

title: Java-to-3T protein corridor (own the logistics where infrastructure is weak)
deciding_reason: The only idea on the programme's growth edge with a real logistics gap, but median is about $14M and the upside is about $90M, short of both bars, with the key rules still undefined.

title: Kitchen workforce employer-of-record: the liability BGN cannot take
deciding_reason: Net take is $4-8k per kitchen, the fee is not an at-cost line, BGN already pays the BPJS premium, and EWA and payroll fintechs exist.

title: Mitra resolution operator: the special servicer banks and BGN cannot be
deciding_reason: Small bank-financed pool, closed kitchens unpaid, the flat incentive is gone, and the problem is a one-off wave, small even in the upside.

title: Telur Koperasi: farmer-cooperative egg grading, pasteurising and glut-buffer plant
deciding_reason: HAP caps any premium, the programme wants direct farmer-to-kitchen sales, the state is building its own egg-powder plant, and the industrial market is small.

title: Dapur Utilitas: IPAL, gas and water as a per-portion service
deciding_reason: Price exceeds value for IPAL, gas is a thin pass-through against state-owned suppliers, and the counterparty's income was just reset.

title: Custody Mutual: jail-health liability program priced on clinical process data
deciding_reason: Insurable pool is about $0.3-0.4B; $100M GWP is 25-30% share and only about $15-20M of MGA revenue; the data and privilege premises are fragile.

title: Outside Care Plan: the DOC's own off-site health plan
deciding_reason: Real budget line and pain, but states already hold carve-outs, Medicaid rates and TPAs, 2026 buyers replaced vendors instead of restructuring, and risk-bearing needs licensure and capital for a 5-8% margin.

title: Clinical Corps: pre-cleared nurse and tele-psychiatry pool
deciding_reason: Corrections staffing already exists and is bid competitively; the idea itself rates the moat weak and copyable in 6-12 months.

title: Piggyback Prime: the first cooperative contract for jail medical services
deciding_reason: A prime that holds the contract and the liability is just a new thin-margin Wellpath; $8-12M net on $100M gross by its own math, and operators will not subcontract to a rival.

title: Day 91: reentry care organization that starts inside the walls
deciding_reason: Real Medicaid-paid benefit, but FQHCs, CBOs, plans and vendors already deliver it, the release-date pipe is built into the waivers, and the payer and federal funding can walk.

title: Cure Carve-Out: high-cost drugs out of the per-diem
deciding_reason: A finite, mostly pass-through $0.9B one-time pool with a 6-10% fee that a pending federal subscription bill would bypass.

title: Day 21: forensic capacity for court-ordered competency restoration
deciding_reason: Court mandate, an existing HHSC private-bed budget line, proven category scale and a state build cost far above a contracted bed; thin moat and Fifth Circuit risk are the open issues.

title: Open-Book Health Authority: fee-only management for counties that lost their vendor
deciding_reason: The model already exists inside Wellpath, the fee pool is a small percentage of each county budget, and county-by-county sales cannot reach $100M of money the company keeps.

title: Second Look: independent per-case SNAP accuracy layer
deciding_reason: Best idea in pool: hard-dollar dated cliff and named signer. But SAS, Maximus and Deloitte are already in states, and observed state contracts are $0.4-4M, so median misses $20M and the $100M upside needs 5-10x current spend.

title: Medicaid-Pending Bridge for nursing homes
deciding_reason: Why-now is thin (one month of retro reach-back), PointClickCare and Optum already sell the service, and even the upside is under $50M.

title: Continuity Manager: PMPM carve-out for the top Medicaid plans
deciding_reason: Real buyers and a funded rival already selling to plans; price per member-year exceeds the contribution margin of the members it retains, so the pool is half the claim and the upside tops out near $60M.

title: Hours Marketplace: verified shifts for the 80 hours
deciding_reason: Demand is tiny against KFF and Georgia data, host capacity is unfunded, verification vendors already exist, and compelled-service employee status is a liability tail. Even the upside is about $30M.

title: Open Verification Exchange with a cheapest-first router
deciding_reason: Consent-based competitors already hold state contracts (Washington, Missouri) at lower prices, states and integrators already orchestrate cheap sources first, and a router is a thin layer with a ceiling near $50M.

title: Renewal Autopilot priced per auto-completed case
deciding_reason: Ten incumbents already pledged free or discounted help on the same systems the vendor needs access to; no outcome-pricing precedent; the idea's own $100M path needs heroic share.

title: Exemption Evidence Utility, starting with medical frailty
deciding_reason: A free product from the vendor states already pay covers the code-set half, the clinician half is a thin-margin services network, and the idea's own total is only about $100M at near-total adoption.

title: Rules Twin: versioned rules and a caseload digital twin
deciding_reason: Open-source and nonprofit rules-as-code already exist, buyers have project budgets not recurring lines, and the idea's own path needs about 70% of states.

title: Slot Book: block-booked engine shop capacity for mid-tier operators
deciding_reason: Premise contradicted: no binding capacity product is evidenced, parts rather than slots gate turnaround, and even the pitch's own math needs 26-32% share; upside is about $35M.

title: The Repair Library: approved-repair IP for engine piece parts
deciding_reason: Real pain but scaled incumbents (Chromalloy 50+ DER repairs on the same parts, HEICO) and heavy capital; median about $10M, upside about $80M.

title: Fleet Buying Group: a Vizient for aircraft maintenance with PMA offtake pools
deciding_reason: AAR Airvoyant and SkySelect are shipping the pitch's year-2 product, the only aviation GPO precedent is dead, and OEM sole-source pricing limits pooled leverage; upside about $35M.

title: Graded Parts: authentication, escrow and indemnity for non-OEM parts
deciding_reason: Authentication layer is occupied and funded; indemnity layer has no evidenced insurer or loss data; realistic fee base is a few percent of a small USM pool.

title: Kit-First: induct the kit, not the engine
deciding_reason: FTAI already runs this as a profitable module factory and sells to third parties; the entrant has the forecast but not the parts. Gross profit upside is about $22M.

title: Shop-Floor Ledger: evidence capture the MRO ERPs cannot do
deciding_reason: A $100M outcome would exceed Ramco's whole revenue; the space is funded and consolidating under IFS and AVIATAR; matches the generic AI copilot cliche. Upside about $20M.

title: Engine Lifeline: flexible-term spare-engine cover pool for institutional owners
deciding_reason: Cleanest payer and fee pool in the pool, but short-term cover and third-party engine capital already exist at scale and the why-now is the crowding signal; median about $12M, upside about $75M.

title: Certifier Capacity: portable-authorization travel certifiers
deciding_reason: Aviation staffing is already done at scale; revenue can pass $100M but net economics are staffing-grade with no moat; upside net revenue about $25M.

title: Last Mile: a locate-first, net-recovery operator for the default chain
deciding_reason: Only idea with an existing budget line, easy bake-off switching and a $100M gross path from 3-4 anchor lenders; but incumbents sell every component except net-proceeds pricing, so upside is borderline and the median is soft.

title: Downshift: a lender-approved short-payoff and trade-down exchange
deciding_reason: Most non-obvious idea and a real loss-mitigation insight, but the lender gain depends on dealers overpaying wholesale and adoption is slow; median is far below $20M.

title: Policy Escrow: the car's insurance inside the car payment
deciding_reason: Real pain but the payer is a carrier commission, the only named competitor is not an escrow, and the business reduces to insurance distribution with weak retention and no lender budget.

title: Driveway in a Box: a captive finance arm for mid-size dealer groups
deciding_reason: Already done by Octane since Jan 2026, and even at 100% of the large-group universe the platform fee does not reach $100M.

title: Payday Rail: lender-paid, payday-aligned payments with portable mandates
deciding_reason: A feature, not a company: funded processors and paycheck-linked vendors already sell it and pricing would compress to cents.

title: Independent Servicer of Record ('Cenlar for auto')
deciding_reason: Largest reachable wallet but crowded with funded and captive-affiliated servicers; a de novo entrant's upside is about $70M, below the bar.

title: Pledge Registry: a neutral cross-lender collateral ledger with an insured certificate
deciding_reason: The gap claim is false: funded competitors with bank investors already run cross-lender checks, and the wallet is far below $100M.

title: Seasoned-Paper Exchange: sell the loans that survived a year
deciding_reason: Heroic share (a third of an assumed flow), premise that credit unions buy BHPH paper is unverified, and liquidity incumbents already serve dealers.

title: Approved-Claim Notes
deciding_reason: Already done and funded by SquareDash and iink, which also own the endorsement rail; the payment-delay premise is overstated; and a lender's revenue is capital-bound, so even the upside is under $100M.

title: Restoration RCM
deciding_reason: Largest real wallet in the batch, but the wedge segment is already served by funded software, the percentage-of-collections price is roughly 2x the in-house cost, and median stays under $20M.

title: Storm Pro Co-op
deciding_reason: False size premise: total roof replacement value is $23B including labor, so the $100M path needs over half of insured roofing materials, and manufacturer rebates already occupy the fee.

title: Pay-in-Five Managed Repair
deciding_reason: Well-funded, entrenched incumbents sell to the same signer; the $100M path exceeds Crawford's scale; and the pay-in-five leg is a lender.

title: Claims Escrow Co.
deciding_reason: The float premise is contradicted by primary Fannie text and AB 493, the servicer remains liable and holds custody by rule, and iink already sits in the workflow; pool without float is at most $120M at full share.

title: Mid-Band Advocate
deciding_reason: The fee-on-whole-settlement math is internally inconsistent with the $1-4k uplift and is restricted or barred in several states; contractors supplement for free; median is far below $20M.

title: Fire and Smoke Program
deciding_reason: The clearance standard does not exist until 2027-2029, the 13,000 LA files are likely outside the new law, and the payer is the conflicted insurer; national path rests on other states copying California.

title: Certified Complete
deciding_reason: The pool is inflated several-fold, and verified-capture vendors with Verisk and Cotality distribution plus iink already sell loss-draft inspection workflow.

title: Coverage Continuity Desk: servicer-paid, borrower-aligned replacement for lender-placed tracking
deciding_reason: No budget line: tracking is funded by LPI, fee-based trackers already exist, the cure benefits the borrower not the servicer, and per-loan pricing exceeds the value of a service touching about 3% of loans.

title: Placement Desk: pay for the agent's hour (distressed-risk exchange for FAIR, E&S and take-out carriers)
deciding_reason: Core product already launched by a funded wholesaler (Bridge) and automation vendors; $100M is 26-40% of the wholesale layer; pool may shrink as admitted carriers return.

title: Proceeds Desk: custody, draws and contractor fast-pay for insurance money
deciding_reason: Shock and law are real, but three funded or entrenched loss-draft vendors exist, the payer pays BPO prices not $600, and the upside needs a lending balance sheet.

title: Closing Desk: outcome-priced total-loss claim operation with a regulatory warranty
deciding_reason: A better-run TPA in a market with Pilot, Sedgwick and well-funded Reserv; the warranty is worth little; median falls just under the $20M floor and upside under $100M.

title: Soft-Landing Exchange: outplacement for non-renewed policyholders, sold to the carrier that is leaving
deciding_reason: Best structural upside in the pool (recurring commission, owned channel) but no carrier has been shown willing to sign, free substitutes sit in every notice, and median is far under the $20M floor.

title: Draw and Price Oracle: the conflict-free percent-complete and paid-invoice price standard (weakest, flagged)
deciding_reason: Idea concedes it cannot reach $100M alone, and a neutral price-data entrant (itel Total Price) already launched inside Xactimate.

title: Rebuild Velocity: an insurer-paid owner's rep priced on ALE months saved
deciding_reason: Conflict of interest (fee rises as ALE shrinks, insurer is payer), existing end-to-end builder, and a one-time LA pool.

title: Defensible-Space Network: annual, verified, route-dense fire-hardening subscription
deciding_reason: Mandate is real but price exceeds value, free and incumbent substitutes are everywhere, and a landscaping-margin subscription is a roll-up, not a defensible exchange.

title: Werkhof
deciding_reason: Succession-only funnel needs 5-45% of reachable buildings; tax logic favours the owner keeping the building; specialists start at EUR 10M tickets, so small tickets are capital-heavy with unproven yield and rent is not business-scale revenue.

title: Verkaufsreif
deciding_reason: Best fee model in the pool, but capped by about 10,800 outside sales a year and free chamber and exchange substitutes; ceiling around $50M with disintermediation risk after free prep.

title: Meisterwerk
deciding_reason: Only idea with a proven, named route to $100M revenue, a verified legal premise and abundant sellers; weaknesses are thin margin, a price gap versus owner expectations, and no deep moat.

title: Netzplan
deciding_reason: DSOs keep planning in-house, the outsourced pool is a fraction of the stated one, and funded generalist engineering roll-ups are already buying the same retiring offices.

title: Teamkauf
deciding_reason: Even the upside is about $38M: employee takeovers are about 6,300 a year and personal liability on 077 deters the very employees it targets; pieces of the stack already exist.

title: Aufloesungsboerse
deciding_reason: Per-client revenue is small, fee payers are scarce, free substitutes cover each piece, and the Sec. 613a workaround is fragile; even the upside is under $30M.

title: Zulieferwerk
deciding_reason: Demand to Mittelstand machinists is unproven until 2027 data, the market is a closed shop, no prime commitment exists, and PE already bids for defence-adjacent shops.

title: Anschluss
deciding_reason: Small connections are worth little, developers already trade connected land, and the $100M path is just a property fund.

title: Signed-Off: the QA-accountable AI engineering house
deciding_reason: Best-sized, budgeted market with a testable 90-day pilot and no one found selling fixed-price QA-owned AI deliverables; but QA exclusivity is overstated and Enercon can copy, so the edge is AI-native economics.

title: Dose Ledger: the nuclear traveler network
deciding_reason: Real shortage but commodity staffing at 15-20% margin against Westinghouse/BHI, D&Z and a venture-funded TNC; $100M needs heroic share.

title: Certified Cell: Hadrian for nuclear (the automated NQA-1 parts factory)
deciding_reason: Good structure but crowded by better-capitalized buyers, demand beyond conditional AP1000 loans unproven, and the pitched pool relied on a loan misread as a parts budget.

title: One Audit: a supplier-paid shared accreditation for nuclear (Nadcap for nuclear)
deciding_reason: Small even in the upside case: the entire aerospace analog earns $70M and the nuclear supplier base is roughly a tenth of what was assumed.

title: Day Rate: the performance-priced outage prime
deciding_reason: Incumbents already sell the same insight; fee pool was fleet-wide savings mistaken for one prime's take.

title: Second Source: HEICO for nuclear plants
deciding_reason: Already done by scaled players, and small even in the upside; 50.69 shrinks the premium further.

title: Uprate Kit: the fixed-price uprate integrator
deciding_reason: Window is narrow and owner-controlled; the only $100M version is a balance-sheet EPC, which a startup cannot credibly be.

title: Clock Keeper: pay-on-approval licensing for the 12- and 18-month NRC clocks
deciding_reason: Small, premise partly wrong, no moat, and AI drafting is already funded; best folded into idea 1 as a developer-facing line.

title: Badge-to-Bill: pre-payment hours integrity for T&M and cost-type labor invoices
deciding_reason: Evidence is a 2012 audit, the EO shrinks the pool over the ramp, there is no agency data-access path or budget line, and even the upside is about $40M.

title: The subcontract rail: Textura for federal services
deciding_reason: Crowded compliance tier, a pay rail already regulated by the 15-day rule, and the Textura take-rate benchmark caps the upside near $60M.

title: The Acceptance Rail: per-event verification for outcome-priced federal contracts
deciding_reason: No budget line, existing QASP tools, and a standard is not something a vendor can mandate; even the upside is small.

title: Verified-WIP lender: control the repayment channel for fixed-price federal work
deciding_reason: Already done by contract-based advance lenders, the government's own milestone financing removes much of the need, and the model is a balance-sheet business with thin moat.

title: The Evidence Desk: ex-auditors who cannot audit, for the 2028 DoD clean-opinion deadline
deciding_reason: Small pool dominated by large firms, DoD building the capability in-house, no real moat, and even the upside is about $40M.

title: The cost-guaranteed sub that primes buy to reprice their own contracts
deciding_reason: Largest honest upside in the pool, but primes already pursue this in-house, the median misses $20M, and the thesis depends on policy surviving 2029.

title: The Outcome Catalog: unit-priced deliverables under the simplified threshold
deciding_reason: The sub-SAT band is built for small business and the plan outgrows it; the lead SKU deflates with FedRAMP 20x tooling; thousands of small shops sell the same thing.

title: Award Ops: outcome-priced grant operations for offices that lost their staff
deciding_reason: The bottleneck is political review, not mechanical checks, the contractor pool is smaller than assumed, and agencies have a free shared service.

title: Lab Order Rail
deciding_reason: Health Gorilla has run the identical free-to-doctor, lab-pays-per-order model since 2014 and ELLKAY sells eligibility at order; the $0.40-0.80 fee is 3-20x e-prescribing network fees, so upside is under $40M.

title: Know-Before-You-Bill
deciding_reason: Real pain, but the appeal and prevention fee base is a thin slice of collections, XiFin holds the data and 73% of large labs, and funded AI-RCM entrants are already in; $100M needs 8-18% of the pool.

title: Telelab
deciding_reason: The only evidence puts the saving near 12.76 net hours a month against a $100k+ price, an on-site tech is still needed, and the rule is a proposal that does not clearly enable a contractor model; upside about $30M.

title: Lab Switch
deciding_reason: The savings are real but Avalon, carriers and Quest already sell lab steering through the same TPA and broker channel; $100M needs about 20M lives at a fee employers can get free from their carrier.

title: Outreach Without Selling
deciding_reason: Biggest pool with real velocity (Quest and Labcorp buying about $1B a year), a proven independent-operator model (PAML) and no operator left; only strong in the restructured JV form because an 8% fee cannot fund the operations.

title: Third Lab
deciding_reason: Revenue is buyable but the moat is not: Quest and Labcorp outbid for the same assets, Sonic and BioReference show the third-national path stalling, and no payer commitment exists.

title: Hospital Lab Gain-Share Desk
deciding_reason: Per-hospital gain-share is a few hundred thousand dollars, consultants and Quest/Labcorp already serve the same CFO, and the idea scored itself weak on moat; upside about $40M.

title: Lab OS for Small Labs
deciding_reason: Director services already sell for under $30k a year per lab, the five-lab cap forces headcount, and the multi-site customer base is tiny; upside about $20M.

title: Seam Map
deciding_reason: Real pain and real budget, but the $40k recurring price is unsupported, Risklytics already sells the core, and free broker and counsel analysis cap the market.

title: Warranty File
deciding_reason: Sharpest insight in the pool (claims die by rescission), but the evidence layer is already built, insured-side price exceeds value, and no carrier has agreed to waive rescission.

title: The Mutual
deciding_reason: Biggest pool, but only 3-5 whale buyers who can self-insure, and the best-funded would-be builder (AIUC) wrote the proposal; manager fee, not gross premium, is the revenue.

title: Gate Meter
deciding_reason: Good pattern transfer from usage-based auto, but it is a pricing method rather than a moat, replicable by funded rivals, and the gateway channel is the weakest link.

title: Waive List
deciding_reason: Small even in the upside, treaty premise unverified, and carriers' existing data vendors and plain application questions are the obvious substitutes.

title: Mirror Policy
deciding_reason: Genuine unserved BI/PD gap, but the author's own math caps AI-only below $100M, primaries can sell back, and the wrap-everything stretch is a different, more crowded business.

title: Causation Desk
deciding_reason: Central legal analogy fails and the buyer prefers silence; at best a $10-20M expert-services practice.

title: Trigger
deciding_reason: Occupied by Parametrix, and sized against a cat-bond market about 100x too small for the $5B referenced limit.

title: Lot-Lender
deciding_reason: Park-lender contracts and a lender community channel already exist (21st Mortgage, Zippy), capital is flooding in (Pretium/Cascade, Saluda/Zippy), and the one new claim, that rent ledgers beat FICO, is untested.

title: Open Lot
deciding_reason: Revenue is easy but the moat is not: manufacturers with captive plants, lenders and cash are already buying the same independents, and independents already shop lenders. A distribution roll-up with thin margins.

title: Park Shield
deciding_reason: MSI, backed by Baldwin Group, launched park-lease embedded insurance 18 days ago, Triad and others already sell it, and MGA commission cannot reach $100M of revenue.

title: Park Utility Co
deciding_reason: The payer is one-time grants that are shrinking, a utility charge is a rent increase by another name, and even a third of visible grant money is about $50M.

title: Covenant Parks
deciding_reason: Real gap with no scaled for-profit covenant owner found, counter-positioned against REIT rent growth, tailwinds intensifying, and the $100M path survives at corrected numbers. Price-to-return is the open risk.

title: Deposit Bridge
deciding_reason: Credit unions already have a top-five chattel lender and Triad markets to them; the $6B managed book is unsourced and heroic. Even a $3B book yields about $55M.

title: Title I Reborn
deciding_reason: Premise is false on primary data: Ginnie manufactured-housing MBS is only $92M and shrinking, and Title I cover is capped at 10% of a lender's portfolio, so it does not convert chattel into a Treasury-linked asset.

title: Keyring
deciding_reason: Works inside REIT parks; outside them it adds park-remittance risk, rent-to-own law exposure and a thin spread, and 21st Mortgage already funds infill for park owners.

title: National ESA provider network (Forage + CAQH + Headway for ESA vendors)
deciding_reason: Payers own vendor lists by statute, payout is already 2-10 days, and the realistic ceiling is about $40M even if states cooperate.

title: School payments and capital OS (Toast for private schools and microschools)
deciding_reason: Real pain but half the cash is front-loaded, no assignable receivable, and FACTS/Nelnet owns the schools and a balance sheet. Upside depends on platforms' cooperation.

title: K-12 education wallet and custody (HealthEquity for scholarship dollars)
deciding_reason: Best premise and ceiling, but median is about $13M and $100M needs Treasury-scale giving, about 30% share and contested yield retention together.

title: SGO host (Fidelity Charitable for scholarships)
deciding_reason: Already done: ACE's EmpowerEd is a free white-label host for the same affiliates with a 25-year donor base. Upside under $40M.

title: Neutral eligibility and anti-duplication clearinghouse (National Student Clearinghouse for K-12 scholarships)
deciding_reason: The rule's wallet safe harbor bundles duplicate control, the recipient base is small, and payers have no budget line; NSC's analog took 30 years.

title: Family-facing funding stack and net-price front door (Common App for choice dollars)
deciding_reason: A funnel, not a business: FACTS Grant & Aid, FACTS Compass and ACE already route families, SGOs get applicants from schools and parishes, and the idea concedes it feeds ideas 3 and 5.

title: Permitted-seat platform (E-occupancy landlord and turnkey seats)
deciding_reason: Real capacity shortage but revenue is rent on about $1.6B of real estate, Primer already sells such buildings, and demand depends on one state's budget.

title: Credit concierge (free planning tool for tax professionals and payroll, paid by SGOs)
deciding_reason: Channel is already addressed by ACE's advisor partner programme at 3%, donors give by affinity not accountant choice, and 6% is too heavy for a 10% overhead.

title: Parity
deciding_reason: Real but small: conversion budgets cap per-event fees at about 10% of all-in cost, vendors and challengers are building AI migration themselves, and the Sunset volume it depends on is dead. Upside about $60M.

title: Tenancy
deciding_reason: Best-structured idea and demand is proven, but the proof is incumbents: CU*Answers and Aux/CU Service Network already do it, and $100M means out-scaling a 50-year-old CUSO in six years. Upside about $65M.

title: Quorum
deciding_reason: Author concedes likely dead standalone; consultants and Paladin already own the pricing data and sell to the bank side; vendor-paid lead budgets are small. Small even in the upside.

title: Sunset
deciding_reason: The vendor tried this sunset, lost clients, and publicly renounced it; one buyer; no announced retirement anywhere. The premise that makes it big is false.

title: Books of Record
deciding_reason: Crowded sidecar category with funded players, small current instant-payment volume, and the expansion step is just becoming a core. Upside about $45M.

title: Day One
deciding_reason: Attrition pain is real but the connections leg is sold by funded switchers inside the digital vendors, and sizable M&A events number about 100 a year. Best as a module of a larger offer; upside about $40M.

title: Switchboard
deciding_reason: Cleanest payer and a credible audit wedge, but the cooperative layer and cost-based pricing already exist (Velera, SHAZAM), consultants sell the audit, and the net margin is assumed. Upside about $60M.

title: Bureau
deciding_reason: A financing play in a space deep-pocketed PE already works; multiples are double the pitch; the edge is capital, not product. Not a venture a founder can start.

title: Gap Ledger
deciding_reason: A feature with free substitutes (lender calculators, Workday cap logic, Juno, in-house RFPs), and the entire school buydown fee pool is smaller than the revenue target. The $100M is another idea's balance sheet.

title: Seasoning Factory
deciding_reason: Best of pool and a genuine capital-and-data gap, but no verified edge over Nelnet, KKR and Ascent's own ABS, and net revenue upside (~$55M) is about half the bar. First-loss capital is a precondition, not an outcome.

title: Offer-Backed
deciding_reason: Carrot-only employer design is a real insight, but the lending half rests on an unsupported credit claim, the employer half belongs to funded incumbent Clasp, and volumes are unsourced.

title: Operator Rail
deciding_reason: The anchor operator already announced a Sallie Mae loan-cap partnership with a capital syndicate, and the above-cap graduate starts needed for $100M cannot be shown.

title: Program Score Exchange
deciding_reason: Too few payers, free federal substitutes, and a revenue sum that assumes near-universal adoption and unusually high data fees.

title: Employer-Cohort Cap-Fit
deciding_reason: The cap-fit price already exists at scale (WGU with hospital partners), the OPM model is the one that is failing, and $100M needs 100+ programs.

title: Earnings Replica
deciding_reason: ED already published the program-level estimates free, the consent-based sample is statistically weak and IVES-constrained, and only ~6% of programs are exposed.

title: Verified-Pay Part-Timer
deciding_reason: Capital-heavy unsecured lending with unsourced volume, no moat (payroll APIs are sold to all lenders), and net upside around $25M.

title: One Knock: the annual home check that replaces six statutory visits and fixes what it finds
deciding_reason: The one-visit bundle is already sold by Sureserve and tendered as combined lots; EICR cycle mismatch and a nearly spent catch-up wave leave thin differentiation.

title: Hot-Spot Contract: capitated root-cause care for the worst 5-8% of homes
deciding_reason: Only idea where no one was found taking capitated risk on the costliest homes; budget lines exist, skew is plausible, and a data/reinsurance asset gives a scale route; kill test still open.

title: Clock Desk: pay per closed Awaab case, not per hour
deciding_reason: Case count is 3-5x too high on real data, the idea's own path is heroic share, and frameworks, law-firm tools and in-house teams already occupy the space.

title: Home Safety Technician Guild: the scarce input behind every other idea
deciding_reason: Already done by employers and academies, no scale asset beyond headcount, and the idea itself concedes a weak moat that dies if the shortage eases.

title: Void Clock: the one party paid for the days between tenants
deciding_reason: Real budget line and signer, but bundled fixed-rate voids and void KPIs already exist, the days gap is smaller on the right baseline, and most revenue is pass-through works with no moat beyond process.

title: Decant Reserve: idle void days and block-leased units as the supply landlords and councils cannot trade
deciding_reason: In-pool market is tiny and already served by own-void licences; the $100M path needs temporary accommodation, where institutional capital and long leases are crowding out nightly-paid void-gap supply.

title: Falls on a Clock: standard adaptations delivered inside the Awaab deadline
deciding_reason: Small in-pool, the DFG bridge is council-controlled and thin-margin, and the one proof point (Millbrook) is mis-cited.

title: Whole-Home Once: one disturbance per home instead of five component programmes
deciding_reason: Real budget and a plausible visit-count insight, but offsite whole-home delivery has scaled slowly everywhere, the upside needs 5x Europe's annual pace, and execution/working-capital risk is severe.

title: Girvi Formalizer
deciding_reason: Biggest pool and no direct competitor, but the savings premise is unproven for rate-capped licensed pawnbrokers, the gold-book buyer field is crowded, and a competent upside is about $60M gross interest income.

title: Bullion-Bid
deciding_reason: Auction flow tracks NPAs, which are falling; e-auction vendors and lender portals already exist; the pitch's own $100M needs 40% of a stress-year flow. Small even in the upside.

title: Karat Ledger
deciding_reason: Real mandate and real appraiser fraud, but large lenders run in-house audit, LMS vendors already hold collateral records and XRF is cheap; the warranty line is inflated 10-50x. Tops out near $60M; the pool itself calls it a wedge.

title: Gold Float
deciding_reason: Axis built it in-house through its own Freecharge subsidiary; UPI credit lines are banks and SFBs only; revolving consumption lines conflict with the 12-month bullet cap. Small even in the upside.

title: Switch Desk
deciding_reason: Real price gap and a real maturity-date hook, but lenders already run balance transfers, the gap is smaller than pitched, fees are DSA-sized, and the honest upside is below $100M.

title: Co-Lend Exchange
deciding_reason: Author concedes it is dead stand-alone; bilateral gold co-lending and Yubi Co.Lend occupy it; 80:20 is the old model; $100M needs 45% of the NBFC book. Small even in the upside.

title: Renewal Wall Cure Desk
deciding_reason: False premise: lower-of-30-day-average valuation means the one-day 29 Jan spike barely entered valuations, so the renewal shortfall is about 0-10%, not 12-23%; stress is not visible and the why-now window is short.

title: Gold Bay
deciding_reason: Strong-room fit-out is a commodity; entrants buy branches instead of building; the INR 9 lakh price is unsupported and $100M needs about 100% of the entrant wave.

title: The Meter: client-owned proof of what offshore vendors actually delivered
deciding_reason: Governance, invoice validation and vendor-output measurement are already sold by ISG, Avasant, ServiceNow, CAST and BlueOptima at about 0.7% of spend; the novel telemetry join is real but is best an evidence layer, not a standalone $100M company.

title: Penny-Exact: independent proof that the AI-translated system behaves identically
deciding_reason: Best why-now and a real data asset, but AWS, Mechanical Orchard and Cognition bundle verification and no regulator mandates independent certification, so the payer budget is unproven; median stays under the $20M bar.

title: The Middle: a sponsor-level AI-native maintenance utility for PE portfolios
deciding_reason: Services revenue could reach $100M, but the sponsor channel is now contested by $1.5B and $4B AI-services ventures and nothing in the model scales beyond labor arbitrage (no software, data or standard).

title: Clawback: an IT-services contract recovery factory with claims financing
deciding_reason: Already done by Vaudit and PRGX, the idea itself calls its moat the weakest of the eight, and the fee pool needs 13%+ share even at an unproven 3% leakage; small even in the upside.

title: Run-Base Shrinker: an energy-services company for the application estate
deciding_reason: Only idea that reverses the buyer's incentive (paid from audited ledger savings, self-funding, vendor-neutral) with a named payer and a path to 6% of a $1.7B shared-savings pool; main risks are testable cheaply.

title: Evergreen Release Utility: flat-price release remediation, Guidewire first
deciding_reason: Already contested by integrator factories, Guidewire-specific AI test tools and a $60M-funded Tessera; spend base looks inflated against $2.2M average ARR; upside tops out near $65M.

title: The Foundry: wholesale AI-native delivery for the incumbents
deciding_reason: Counter-positioning logic is clever but incumbents are buying tools and embedded engineers directly; a single-anchor wholesale model tops out near $70M and sits on a delivery head's P&L.

title: Hot Spare: shadow-sourcing as a service
deciding_reason: The regulation requires tested exit plans, not a paid shadow vendor, so a cheap tabletop satisfies it; the buyer pays twice for the shadowed work and dual sourcing already exists; small even in the upside.

title: Dock Crews with a Turn-Time Guarantee
deciding_reason: Real payer and price signal, but loading minutes are collapsing without a crew business, Timee and 3PLs already sell the hours, and revenue is staffing-margin pass-through (about 15% gross).

title: Open-Book Tier-1: Floor Plus Ten Percent, Carriers Free, Paid in Three Days
deciding_reason: The owner-backed leader did this for six years and is small; the open-book fee is a copyable pricing tactic; the $100M fee path needs about 60x the best precedent at roughly 4% contribution.

title: The Anchor Roll-Up: Buy the Permits the Cost Floor Will Strand
deciding_reason: Revenue is bought, not earned: at a 1.0% sector margin the median case earns almost nothing, permits are not scarce, strategics already buy, and the cost floor lifts all carriers equally.

title: The Unit-Load Loop: RFID Rental Pallets for the Decade the Government Mandates T11
deciding_reason: Already done by both incumbents; UPR, the number-2 pool, is the $100M business at a 1.8% operating margin; entry costs about $160M of capex for a capital-heavy utility return.

title: The Carrier's Advocate: Contingency Recovery of Price, Waiting and Handling Charges
deciding_reason: Free and subsidised substitutes already exist, contingent negotiation collides with Attorneys Act art. 72, the fee is one-off for 24 months, and the 2028 cost floor will do the job by formula.

title: The Neutral Clean Room for Competing Shippers' Joint Trucks
deciding_reason: Premise false: METI-backed traevo noWa already runs anonymous shipper-to-shipper matching for free, and the Hokkaido pilot shows only 4.7% of registered routes seek a match.

title: The Capacity Reservation Exchange for Shippers Who Cannot Afford a Failed Tender
deciding_reason: Largest real pain of the eight but willingness to pay is untested, there is no moat, the product puts capacity risk on your balance sheet, and Hacobell or a 3PL can copy it once demand is proven.

title: The Relay Exchange: One Contract, One Settlement, Three Carriers
deciding_reason: The largest carriers already run multi-party relays, the state is building hubs and pushing cooperatives as matchers, and the $100M path needs about 10% of a guessed 24M runs.

title: Approved Buyer: a pre-cleared consolidator for rental divestitures, distressed route books and succession sales
deciding_reason: Remedy trigger is speculative and 5+ funded buyers already roll up independents, but acquired-revenue path to $100M needs about 3% of targets; a sharpened, remedy-optional version clears the numeric bar.

title: Rental-grade garments with RFID at the loom: a nearshore mill for everyone who is not Cintas
deciding_reason: Commodity cut-and-sew with $15-20M gross profit even at $100M sales; established laundry suppliers exist; RFID-at-sewing is a sold step, not a moat.

title: The Laundry Foundry: a neutral, automated, PFAS-ready wet-processing hub for rental companies
deciding_reason: No forcing function (no PFAS rule), owners with paid-off plants would sell before they outsource, and about 2x capital per revenue dollar.

title: Route Desk: a managed-service layer for multi-site operators' route-based services
deciding_reason: Needs about 150,000 managed locations at about $660 a year; consultants, member networks and incumbent national-account teams already serve this.

title: The Garment Pool: a third-party fleet of standard garments any rental laundry can lease by the wash (CHEP for workwear)
deciding_reason: Economics do not pencil (18% lease fee vs about 13% owned cost) and pooling already happens inside integrated operators; no third-party lessor exists for a reason.

title: White-label rental for uniform dealers and promotional-product distributors
deciding_reason: Depends on two unbuilt ideas, needs 5,000 dealers, and the smallest accounts are the worst route economics.

title: Route Brokerage: a commission-only, multi-supplier sales force for independents
deciding_reason: Real net revenue is the platform's 30-35% share, so $100M gross is about $30M; independents can simply hire the reps.

title: Clean Effluent: PFAS source control and pretreatment as a per-pound service for textile laundries
deciding_reason: No laundry PFAS limit found, laundries a small PFAS source, apparel bans shrink the stream, and the capex quote is one consultant's number.

title: Counterweight: revenue-cycle management for body-shop chains
deciding_reason: Real pain and budget, but take is capped by recoverable dollars, the MSO tier is about $23B, and the biggest buyers insource; ceiling about $55M.

title: Severity Pool: volume-pooling purchasing group for tier-2/3 auto carriers
deciding_reason: Tier 2/3 is 24% of the market, so $100M exceeds 100% of the corrected repair-leg base ($79M); network setup is already cheap.

title: Cycle Close: outcome-priced total-loss finishing desk
deciding_reason: Lien and title software is crowded and funded; the corrected base is $147M at 100%; a services desk faces offshore BPO and carrier in-house units.

title: Same-Day: delivery-hour parts network with total-cost sourcing and tariff price-lock
deciding_reason: Overstated premise, entrenched neutral-looking incumbents (LKQ, dealers, MSO warehouses) and delivery economics below courier cost.

title: Open Yard: asset-light salvage sales from the tow yard where the car already sits
deciding_reason: Big pool and insurers move volume quickly, but Salvato already runs the model and Copart just bought ACV; buyer depth is the moat.

title: Dent Plan: prepaid repair membership priced off shop slack, not insurance risk
deciding_reason: As designed it is likely insurance; the fix removes the product; revenue is gross and distribution to owners of older cars is weak.

title: Proof Plate: neutral ADAS repair plan and completion record
deciding_reason: The plan layer already exists at $3 a report with an insurer reimbursing it; the legal mandate is glass-only; dispatch upside is capped.

title: Ground Truth: independent audit and sold-price data for total-loss valuations and claims AI
deciding_reason: Self-assessed ceiling $40-60M; sold-price data is licensed from the vendors it would audit; the escape route is a head-on fight with Cox and J.D. Power.

title: Intercompany Reconciler
deciding_reason: Real gap and legal premise hold, but Optravis already sells TP software with customs logic, advisers publish the playbook, and the 2% savings carrying the $100M path is unsupported; honest ceiling is a SaaS-plus-services niche.

title: Rights Ledger
deciding_reason: Legal premise is sound and no cross-company ledger exists, but the base is conflated, the distributor gains nothing, per-client drawback vendors are many, and the upside depends on a court-challenged Section 301 duty.

title: Origin Rail
deciding_reason: Mandated demand (FCA wave, CF-28 volume) is real, but a $20 attestation is not defensible evidence, audits cost far more, and Altana already holds the CBP-facing provenance rail.

title: Licence Bank
deciding_reason: Closest to a mechanical $100M path, but it is a financing story: revenue is bought, PE and three AI-stack entrants already occupy both halves, and the claimed licence scarcity does not cap competitors.

title: Second Filer
deciding_reason: The core differentiator is false: licensed, independent, contingent recovery firms already exist, and the recoverable window is ~1-1.5 years of entries, not five; $100M would be about a quarter of the whole fee pool.

title: Peer Ledger
deciding_reason: Antitrust, discovery and trust problems with pooling competitors' declared values, inflated buyer counts (surety feeds are tens of buyers), and free substitutes; even the pitch's own path needs 27% of importers.

title: Weight Line
deciding_reason: The cliff is real but thin: it excludes chapters 72-76, matters only to SKUs near 15%, redesign is one-time, and 232 rules keep changing; even upside is a niche.

title: Pass-Through
deciding_reason: The one-time pool is mostly already refunded to suppliers, accounting firms and law firms already sell it, big carriers pass refunds through voluntarily, and the author concedes a 2-3 year spike.
